THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the injured petitioner is seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded in M.V.C.No.355/2015 by the learned M.A.C.T., Bangalore City , SCCH-14 ('the Tribunal' in short) by judgment dated 05.12.2016.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts are, on 25.07.2014 at about 7.00 p.m., while the petitioner was walking on the left side of Bangalore-Bellary Main road, opposite to IFA Gate, Yalahanka, Bangalore, a Canter bearing No.KA-42-2087 dashed against her injuring all over body.

She was treated at Baptist Hospital,
Hebbal, NC: 2023:KHC:33630 Bangalore, from 25.07.2014 to 30.07.2014.
Claiming compensation of Rs.10 lakhs, she moved the Tribunal.
The Insurance Company has opposed the claim.
The Tribunal after taking the evidence, by impugned judgment, awarded Rs.1,62,000/- with 9% interest per annum.
Pleading inadequacy
, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.B.Chandrashekaraiah, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.O.Mahesh, learned counsel for respondent No.2/insurer.
5.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries, she was hospitalized for 6 days and laid up for a period of one year.
The Tribunal has not considered the gravity of the injuries and notional income taken at Rs.8,000/- is meager.

The Tribunal has not properly assessed the compensation towards loss of income during treatment,
loss of NC: 2023:KHC:33630 amenities and future medical expenses and sought for re-assessment of the compensation.
6.

Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the petitioner has not produced any evidence to show that injuries have affected her earning capacity nor any evidence about her income and the Tribunal has correctly assessed the notional income of the petitioner and Smt Avvamma vs Hindustan Coco Cola Berverage on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119676572/
2 awarded just compensation and he supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on behalf of both parties and also perused the materials on record.
8.

sentences.text: There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of accident, injuries sustained by the petitioner and her entitlement to claim the compensation.
Petitioner is entitled to just compensation and it shall neither be inadequate nor a bonanza.
The petitioner has not examined treated Doctor to show the disability.

As the accident was in the year 2014, for a person with no proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed not less than Rs.8,500/- per month, whereas the Tribunal has assessed at Rs.8,000/-, which is on the lower side.
The petitioner has suffered head injury and fracture of right clavicle, which will make her to laid up for minimum of six months to resume herself to normal life.
Hence, loss of income during laid-up period of six months has to be calculated.
Head injury certainly requires future medication, but the Tribunal NC: 2023:KHC:33630 did not consider future medical expenses which the petitioner is required to incur.

9. On perusal of the impugned judgment, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the income towards pain and suffering, medical expenses and incidental charges, but it has inadequately awarded compensation towards loss of income during laid-up period.
Hence, it has to be assessed for six months.
Loss of amenities and discomfort ought to have been awarded adequately as against Rs.25,000/- and future medical expenses has to be assessed at Rs.10,000/-.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.15,000/- under the head 'inconvenience', which has no explanation and therefore, it has to be disallowed.
If all these aspects are taken into consideration, it is proper to enhance a sum of Rs.47,000/- as global compensation in addition to what has been assessed by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appeal merits consideration.

In result, the following:
NC: 2023:KHC:33630 ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The impugned judgment and award is modified.
